question: What happens during the oxidation of ethanol?

options.text: It is converted into ethanoic acid.

solution:
The correct answer is __**It is converted into ethanoic acid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The oxidation of **ethanol** (CH₃CH₂OH) is a chemical reaction where it is transformed into **ethanoic acid** (CH₃COOH), also known as **acetic acid**.
 
• This process is carried out using strong **oxidizing agents** such as **alkaline potassium permanganate** (KMnO₄) or **acidified potassium dichromate** (K₂Cr₂O₇).
 
• When **ethanol** is heated with these reagents, the **hydroxyl group** (-OH) is converted into a **carboxyl group** (-COOH). ***Hence, the statement that it is converted into ethanoic acid is correct.***
 
• In this reaction, the addition of **oxygen** and the removal of **hydrogen** take place, which is the fundamental definition of **oxidation** in organic chemistry.
